answer: A hosted-miner network can require every identity to post a refundable bond reclaimable only by a fresh, independently attested payout address, so a dune of cloned keys costs the attacker real capital per seat instead of nothing. Payout waits until the epoch closes, forcing that stake to sit through settlement, and the mirror effect of splitting rewards across near-identical accounts is diluted by the same per-seat bond. Bidding up vote weight with a juniper of identities therefore requires posting the bond once per depositor, so the cost of a Sybil swarm scales with seat count.
